subject: pharmacology
title: Antiepileptic Adverse Effects and Teratogenicity: Gingival Hyperplasia, Fetal Hydantoin and Neural Tube Defects

steps.tx: **Gingival hyperplasia** is phenytoin's signature on the dental chair: painless fibrotic overgrowth of the gums beginning in the interdental papillae within months, worsened by plaque and poor hygiene, milder counterparts trailing cyclosporine and calcium channel blockers in a famous three drug differential. Folate depletion may contribute. Management is oral hygiene obsession, dental referral, dose review and switching agent where epilepsy allows, because surgical debulking without drug change simply regrows.
steps.say: Overgrown gums on phenytoin need the dentist and the drug chart together; surgery alone regrows.

left.title: Drug induced gingival overgrowth trio
points: Phenytoin: the classic, dose and hygiene related
Ciclosporin: transplant populations
Calcium channel blockers: nifedipine and amlodipine
All worsened by plaque accumulation

right.title: Management sequence
points: Intensive oral hygiene and plaque control
Dental review and folate status
Dose reduction or agent switch where possible
Gingivectomy reserved, relapse expected without change

steps.tx: On the dental chair, **gingival hyperplasia** is the mark of phenytoin: painless fibrous overgrowth that begins between the teeth within months and worsens when plaque is left in place. Cyclosporine and calcium channel blockers produce milder versions, and the three drugs form a classic differential. Folate depletion may contribute. Management is strict cleaning, a dental opinion, a look at the dose, and a change of antiepileptic if seizures allow it. Cutting the gums away without changing the drug lets the same overgrowth return.
steps.say: Phenytoin causes painless fibrous gum overgrowth that starts between the teeth within months and is worse with plaque. Cyclosporine and calcium channel blockers cause a milder copy. Hygiene, dental care and a change of drug are required together, because surgery alone is followed by regrowth if phenytoin continues.

vis.alt: Firm fibrotic gum tissue has overgrown the teeth and buried the interdental papillae.
vis.caption: Painless fibrous gingiva has swollen from the papillae and crept over the crowns, the overgrowth typical of phenytoin. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Fetal hydantoin syndrome** names the phenytoin exposed child's pattern: prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, craniofacial features (broad nasal bridge, hypertelorism, short neck), nail and distal phalanx hypoplasia, and developmental delay, attributed partly to epoxide metabolites and folate antagonism. Modern framing avoids implying certainty per child (many exposed children are unaffected) while keeping the counselling duty. Carbamazepine carries its own smaller craniofacial and neural tube ledger below.
steps.say: Fetal hydantoin is a pattern, not a prophecy; counsel the pattern and plan the pregnancy before it starts.

nodes.label: Epoxide metabolites and folate antagonism implicated
Growth restriction, craniofacial and nail hypoplasia pattern
Preconception switch and folate reduce the risk

steps.tx: **Neural tube defects** distribute across the cabinet with valproate carrying the heaviest share (1 to 2 percent, spina bifida predominating), carbamazepine around 0.5 to 1 percent, and lamotrigine and levetiracetam near background in registry data. Folic acid supplementation (higher dose 5 mg in many guidelines for antiepileptic users) begins before conception because the tube closes by day 28, usually before pregnancy is recognised; supplementation after that date decorates rather than prevents.
steps.say: The tube closes by day twenty eight; folate is a preconception drug or it is a garnish.

left.title: Neural tube defect risk ladder
points: Valproate: 1 to 2 percent, dose related
Carbamazepine: about 0.5 to 1 percent
Lamotrigine and levetiracetam: near background rates
Background population risk about 0.1 percent

right.title: Prevention choreography
points: Folate 5 mg daily before conception in many guidelines
Lowest effective monotherapy dose
Anomaly scanning at 18 to 20 weeks
Registry enrolment offered for outcome data

steps.tx: **Neural tube defects** fall unevenly across antiepileptic drugs. Valproate carries about 1 to 2 percent risk, and spina bifida is the usual defect. Carbamazepine sits near 0.5 to 1 percent. Registry data place lamotrigine and levetiracetam close to the background rate. The higher folic acid dose of 5 mg, advised in many guidelines for women taking these drugs, has to begin before conception. The tube closes by day 28, commonly before a missed period is noticed, and folate started after closure does not prevent the defect.
steps.say: Valproate carries roughly a 1 to 2 percent neural tube defect risk, mostly spina bifida. Carbamazepine is nearer 0.5 to 1 percent, while lamotrigine and levetiracetam sit close to background. Five milligrams of folic acid must start before conception, because the tube closes by day 28, often before pregnancy is known.

vis.alt: A risk ladder shows neural tube defect rates near background for lamotrigine, higher for carbamazepine, and highest for valproate.
vis.caption: Neural tube defect risk is drawn as a rising ladder from lamotrigine near the background rate, through carbamazepine, to valproate at the top. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Neurodevelopment** may matter more than anatomy in counselling arithmetic: valproate exposure associates with IQ reductions averaging around 7 to 10 points at higher doses and two to three fold increases in autism spectrum diagnoses in cohort studies, outcomes no scan can exclude at 20 weeks. This is why regulators restrict valproate by programme rather than by leaflet, and why preconception switches need months of seizure stability testing on the new agent before conception is attempted.
steps.say: The valproate conversation is about IQ and autism odds, not only spina bifida; switch early and prove stability first.

nodes.label: Counsel anatomy plus neurodevelopment risks together
Switch agent with months of stability proven
Conceive on lowest effective monotherapy with folate
Levels and anomaly surveillance through pregnancy

steps.tx: **Idiosyncratic reactions** cut across mechanisms and demand recognition drills: Stevens Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis with lamotrigine (titration dependent), carbamazepine (HLA flagged) and phenytoin; DRESS (drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms) arriving at two to eight weeks with fever, rash, eosinophilia and hepatitis; and aplastic anaemia historically chained to felbamate and carbamazepine. Any new rash with mucosal involvement or systemic features on a recent antiepileptic means stop and escalate the same day.
steps.say: Rash plus fever, mucosa or eosinophils on a new antiepileptic is a same day stop and escalate.

left.title: Severe reaction patterns
points: Stevens Johnson and toxic epidermal necrolysis: mucosal, blistering
DRESS: 2 to 8 weeks, fever, eosinophilia, hepatitis
Aplastic anaemia: felbamate and carbamazepine history
HLA B*1502 and A*3101 screening for carbamazepine

right.title: Immediate responses
points: Stop the suspect drug the same day
Dermatology and burns or critical care for skin failure
Never rechallenge after Stevens Johnson or DRESS
Cross reacting aromatic agents avoided (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine care)

steps.tx: **Hyponatraemia, bone disease and endocrine ripples** form the cabinet's slow adverse weather: carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine waste sodium through SIADH like action, enzyme inducers catabolise vitamin D and sex steroids (osteoporosis, contraceptive failure, sexual dysfunction), valproate nudges weight and insulin resistance upward, and gabapentinoids sedate. Annual review measuring sodium on the carbamazepine family, vitamin D and bone health on inducers, and weight and glucose on valproate converts these from examination lists into clinic habits.
steps.say: Sodium, bones, weight and contraception: the annual review is where slow toxicities are caught.

left.title: Slow adverse weather
points: Hyponatraemia: carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, eslicarbazepine
Bone loss: enzyme inducers and valproate
Weight and metabolic gain: valproate, gabapentinoids
Sexual and reproductive effects across the cabinet

right.title: Annual review instruments
points: Sodium, full blood count and liver profile by agent
Vitamin D and densitometry where risk accumulates
Weight, glucose and lipids on valproate
Contraception and pregnancy intention revisited

steps.tx: **Enzyme inducing antiepileptics and contraception** deserve unhurried arithmetic: combined pills, patches, rings and progestogen only pills can fail at standard doses, so guidance favours copper or levonorgestrel intrauterine methods unaffected by induction, or depot and implant strategies with caveats, planned with the same seriousness as seizure control because an unplanned pregnancy on valproate or phenytoin is the catastrophe both clinics exist to prevent. Lamotrigine levels, meanwhile, halve on oestrogen contraceptives, risking breakthrough seizures.
steps.say: Inducers defeat pills in both directions: contraception fails, and oestrogen halves lamotrigine levels.

nodes.label: Intrauterine methods preferred, unaffected by induction
Oestrogen halves lamotrigine: seizure and rash vigilance

steps.tx: **Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP)** completes honest counselling: risk near one per thousand patient years, concentrated in uncontrolled generalised tonic clonic seizures, nocturnal seizures and non adherence, reduced by seizure control, night supervision or listening devices, and adherence support rather than any drug choice. Mentioning SUDEP is now expected practice; the conversation itself improves adherence, which is its own intervention.
steps.say: Name SUDEP, count tonic clonic control, and treat adherence as the modifiable risk it is.

points: Frequent generalised tonic clonic seizures
Nocturnal seizures unwitnessed
Non adherence and abrupt drug cessation
Living and sleeping alone

right.title: Risk reduction conversation
points: Optimise tonic clonic seizure control
Adherence support and supply continuity
Night supervision or detection devices
Document the discussion and the plan
